title: Logged in as admin by injecting into the login form
impact: I put the payload in the email box and got logged in as the admin account without knowing the password. After that I could open the admin panel and see all the users and feedback.
remediation: Build the login query with parameters instead of pasting the email into the SQL string, and validate the input before it reaches the database.

title: Used the product search to dump user records
payload_used: qwert')) UNION SELECT id, email, password, '4', '5', '6', '7', '8', '9' FROM Users--
impact: The search box let me add my own UNION SELECT, so the response came back with user emails and password hashes. That data has nothing to do with products and should never be in a search result.
remediation: Use parameterized queries for the search and give the database account only the permissions it really needs.

title: Got JavaScript to run from the search URL
impact: I put the iframe payload in the search URL and the alert popped up in the browser. Someone could use the same trick to steal a session or take over an account.
remediation: Escape the value that gets shown back on the page and stop bypassing Angular's sanitizer. A strict CSP would also make this harder.

title: Left a script sitting in a product description
impact: I updated a product description through the API and the payload stayed in the database. Juice Shop even confirmed the persisted XSS, so the script would run for anyone who views that product.
remediation: Sanitize the description before saving it and escape it when it is displayed. Don't bypass the framework sanitizer, and only let admins change products.
